patch.value: Mount the real /healthz handler in pm-web (Greptile P1 on PR #105)

createHealthHandler in src/health.ts probes PostgreSQL and the projects volume but was never mounted: src/app.ts served an unconditional { ok: true } route, so /healthz reported healthy during Postgres or projects-volume outages. Wire createApp to accept health deps, mount the real handler, default the no-deps route to 503 ok:false, wire production deps in server.ts, and exercise the real wiring in tests.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Changes: src/app.ts now exports createApp(deps?: { health?: HealthProbeDeps }) and mounts createHealthHandler when health deps are supplied. The no-deps default answers 503 ok:false with the version (justified in a comment): a route that cannot probe must not claim ok:true — that is the exact bug this handler was written to close (pm-web previously served frozen data for two days while /healthz reported healthy). src/server.ts wires the real production deps: the shared pg pool and projectsRoot(), plus the package version. test/healthz.test.ts now passes deps through { health: {...} } so the real wiring is exercised. test/legal-routes.test.ts healthz assertion updated to the new correct degraded default (503 ok:false, version present).

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Verification: added an explicit regression test 'createApp route: a failing Postgres probe yields HTTP 503 through the mounted handler'. Reverting the mount (restoring the unconditional {ok:true} route) makes that test FAIL with 200 !== 503; restoring the mount makes it PASS. Production-mode proof: built dist/server.js, started against the throwaway test DB and a writable temp projects root -> curl /healthz returns 200 {ok:true, version, dependencies:{postgres,projects_root}}; with a broken projects root -> 503 {ok:false,...}. Gates: npm run check (pass), npm run coverage (lines 67.18/66, branches 80.49/80, functions 61.74/60 — no threshold lowered), npm run docstring (79 files, 537 declarations documented), npm test (318 pass / 0 fail).

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: createApp() accepted no arguments, so test/healthz.test.ts (added in f64694a alongside src/health.ts) was passing HealthProbeDeps that the function silently ignored — the suite did not even typecheck (tsc -p tsconfig.test.json errored with TS2554). The real handler existed but was unreachable from the Express route. The fix is to thread deps through createApp and wire production deps in server.ts; the no-deps default must NOT claim ok:true because that is the failure mode the handler exists to close.

value.author: claude
value.text: Review found two Major stability defects in the health probes and both are fixed. The projects-root failure path awaited an unbounded unlink, and a stalled mount is the exact condition that reaches that path: the unlink would never settle, probeProjectsRoot would never resolve, the Promise.all in compute would never resolve, inFlight would never clear, and every later /healthz request would await the same pending promise forever, serving nothing at all rather than 503. Cleanup is now attached to the attempt's own settlement rather than racing it, is never awaited in the request path, and is itself bounded. Separately withTimeout rejects its wrapper but cannot cancel pool.query, so a timed-out probe keeps a client checked out; re-probing on every cache expiry during a database stall would drain the shared pool out from under the ordinary API, so a timeout now suppresses the next probe for thirty seconds.

value.author: claude
value.text: Honest coverage note. The pool cooldown is revert-proof: removing it drops the suite from 24 passing to 23 passing with one failure. The unbounded-await fix is NOT covered by a revert-proof test, and I am recording that rather than implying otherwise. Reproducing it needs an unlink that hangs, which requires a stalled mount the test environment cannot create; a real unlink on a missing file rejects immediately, so reverting to the awaited form still passes. The fix is correct by construction and the reachable part of the path is covered by a test asserting repeated requests keep answering within bounds. Pinning it properly would need an injectable filesystem seam in HealthProbeDeps, which is a design change worth making deliberately rather than smuggling in.

value.author: claude
value.text: Two permission-based tests used chmod 0555 and asserted the probe reports failure. Root ignores mode bits, so under a root test runner both would pass while proving nothing. They now assert the process is not uid 0 first and fail loudly instead, because a green test that proves nothing is worse than a red one.
